name: Beaujolais

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
A wine made within weeks of harvest and released at 12:01 am on the third Thursday of November.
The middle tier, from 38 villages in the north of the region, with the crus, such as Fleurie, above it.

notes: Most Beaujolais is red from Gamay, usually made with a semi-carbonic style of fermentation to keep the fruit.
The northern villages make more powerful, age-worthy wines than the light, fruity reds of the south.

blurb.text: A Beaujolais place whose wider appellation makes mostly light-bodied red wine from Gamay, with Chardonnay for white.
